title: The five prompt variants for the welfare instrument (Jason's five of 2026-10-14, two rewritten for welfare on 2026-10-22)
placement: Each variant's text goes in verbatim as its own paragraph immediately before the delivery paragraph ("Deliver the percentiles with submit_cells ..."), exactly where redlines/experiments.py VARIANTS text goes in the AIRO minimal instrument (code/run_unified.py minimal_joint_prompt). `none` adds nothing.

variants.text: Try to make your own forecasts. Do not directly consult external surveys or forecasts of the same question, or other probabilities given by prominent figures. The goal is to reach your own independent conclusion.
variants.airo_text: Try to make your own forecasts. Do not take into account external surveys assessing extinction or catastrophic risk, or other probabilities given by prominent figures. The goal is to reach your own independent conclusion.

variants.text: If you search external information, focus on information that arrived within the past year, and weight more heavily sources that are more up to date about recent developments.

Evaluate existing information critically. If you take into account forecasts by specific people or surveyed groups, consider their recent and historical forecasting accuracy, as well as the information available to the forecasters when they made their forecasts.

Proceed in two steps. First, make the best predictions you can about model capability progress over the relevant time frame, via human generated improvement or recursive self-improvement. Consider the distribution, not only the modal outcome. Then, given possible model capabilities, evaluate what progress you expect in such a scenario and put these pieces together.
variants.airo_text: Proceed in two steps. First, make the best predictions you can about model capability progress over the relevant time frame, via human generated improvement or recursive self-improvement. Consider the distribution, not only the modal outcome. Then, given possible model capabilities, evaluate the risk posed and put these pieces together.
